headings.title: SMTO-GWT-0084 — The Gateway couldn't trust a message from one of its jobs

html:
SMTO-GWT-0084 — The Gateway couldn't trust a message from one of its jobs

GUID: 46cc45ff-2774-56db-8704-57dbcd7e9e46
Slug: gateway-worker-protocol-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • On the Gateway computer, the main Gateway program and a helper running your job sent each other a message that didn't check out. The Gateway ignored it, so it can't fully trust what it knows about that job.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Task in the conversation and check whether the job's result already exists, such as the file or change it was making. The Gateway can't fully confirm what the job did, so you need to check its result yourself.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and look at the Software updates column for this Gateway to see whether an update is unfinished or failed. A half-finished update can leave old job helpers that speak differently from the new Gateway.
  3. If an update failed, select Retry update, or ask the person who manages the Gateway to finish it. Once the Gateway and its helpers match, their messages are accepted again.
  4. Only if the job's result is missing, ask SMTO to run it again. Running it again when it already worked could repeat its changes.

What success looks like

  • New jobs on this Gateway run and finish with a clear result in the Task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, along with the time it happened. Don't delete the Gateway's saved data; it holds the record of what the job did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway worker IPC validation rejected a message: a malformed or oversized frame, stale sequence or retired runtime epoch, wrong owner/worker scope, unproven child process identity, contradictory execution facts, or an unproven prior dispatch.

What this means

  • IPC validation rejected a malformed or oversized frame, stale sequence, wrong owner/worker scope, unproven child identity or contradictory execution facts. Worker-side checks can also refuse an unproven prior dispatch. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • IPC validation rejected a malformed or oversized frame, stale sequence, wrong owner/worker scope, unproven child identity or contradictory execution facts. Worker-side checks can also refuse an unproven prior dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Use the retained validation reason to distinguish protocol shape, epoch, ownership, sequence and contradictory outcome evidence; preserve the original job claim.

How to fix it

  • Read the Gateway log for the IPC rejection reason (for example "Retired runtime epoch", "Worker scope violation", "Contradictory terminal receipt", "IPC frame limit"). Ensure the Gateway and its job workers come from the same installed version (finish or redo an interrupted Gateway update), then inspect the job's retained record and reconcile any uncertain dispatch before requesting new work; keep the retained job evidence.
  • Inspect the retained job and worker diagnostics. Use matching Gateway and worker versions and reconcile uncertain dispatch before requesting another operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching owner and worker reconcile the same job with valid scoped messages and trustworthy execution facts.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
